column5: GHA VIII (Mazrui, 1993) gives about 10,000 Algerian Muslim deaths for the Setif repression of 05/1945, a figure inside the course's range of 1,000 to 45,000 but stated without a method [CONTESTED]

Mazrui attributes the slogan 'seek ye first the political kingdom' to Nkrumah, notes that independence was necessary but not sufficient, and reads Nkrumah as meaning continental liberation; the course's wording matches. The 'all else will be subtracted' line is Mazrui's own gloss on Ghana and Uganda

Mazrui: Sharpeville (03/1960) taught that Gandhian civil disobedience could not succeed against entrenched white rule; the Angola rebellion followed about a year later and the Portuguese empire collapsed after the coup of 04/1974. Independence dates in Table 5.1: Ghana 06/03/1957, Guinea 02/10/1958, Nigeria 01/10/1960, Tanganyika 09/12/1961, Kenya 12/12/1963, Zambia 24/10/1964, Zimbabwe 18/04/1980, Namibia 21/03/1990

Mazrui lists five traditions of resistance (warrior, jihad, radical Christianity, non-violent mobilisation, guerrilla war); 87,000 Tanganyikans served with the Allies; Churchill and Roosevelt signed the Atlantic Charter in 08/1941; the UN Trusteeship Council lobbied against colonialism. These are an academic framing by one author in a UNESCO volume, not a consensus

GHA VIII Table 5.1 dates Algerian independence 03/07/1962 (the referendum result recognised by France); the course says 05/07/1962 (the day it was proclaimed and celebrated). Both dates are in use; state which one is meant

GHA VIII ch 24-25: 30 states were represented at the Addis Ababa conference opening 23/05/1963 and the Charter was signed on 25/05/1963; Togo (after Olympio's assassination) was not admitted and Morocco refused, and both signed later. So 30 at signing plus Togo and Morocco gives 32, which explains the 32 versus 33 counts in the course

GHA VIII calls Manchester 10/1945 the Fifth Pan-African Congress (over 200 participants, African delegates predominating, Nkrumah and Padmore joint secretaries, DuBois chair); the course's 'fifth' is right and Reader's 'sixth' is wrong

GHA VIII: First Conference of Independent African States, Accra 04/1958, eight states; the OAU set up the African Liberation Committee (nine states, HQ Dar es Salaam) with a voluntary Special Fund and declared 25 May African Liberation Day; the Charter lists seven principles, including territorial integrity of every state (not a pledge to keep colonial borders)

GHA VIII (Asante): sub-Saharan external debt rose from 6 to 32 billion dollars 1970-79 (from World Bank 1981); Africa grew 2 per cent a year in the 1960s against 4.1-7.2 per cent elsewhere; 16 of 25 least-developed countries were African in 1971; ECOWAS founded in Lagos 05/1975 with 16 members. Matches the course; Asante argues regional bodies depended on foreign donors and the Lome Convention
